summary: Private deployment: intermittent decrypt failures during customer-managed AWS KMS rotation (Bank of Northlake)
environment: prod (Private deployment) / AWS us-east-1 customer VPC; Redwood Private release 2.16.3; KMS provider: AWS KMS (customer-managed CMK, alias/bankofnorthlake-redwood-kek)
affected_models: N/A (platform decrypt path affecting multiple services)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reported intermittent decrypt failures after rotating their customer-managed AWS KMS key used by Redwood Private for envelope encryption (KEK/DEK). Failures surfaced as 500s across multiple API routes because several services could not decrypt stored secrets/config blobs.

Customer impact
- ~0.5%–1.2% of requests failed with 500 between 2025-02-18 14:32Z and 2025-02-18 17:10Z.
- Errors clustered after pod restarts/autoscaling (cache cold) and during peak traffic.
- Customer described symptoms as “intermittent authentication failures and sporadic model endpoint errors.”

Environment
- Deployment type: Redwood Private (customer-operated)
- Region: AWS us-east-1
- Redwood version: 2.16.3 (per customer)
- KMS: AWS KMS CMK referenced via alias/bankofnorthlake-redwood-kek
- Rotation action performed by customer: updated KMS key reference in Helm values and restarted services; disabled the prior key within ~30 minutes of cutover.

What changed / timeline (customer-provided)
- 2025-02-18 14:15Z: Created new CMK (or rotated alias target) and updated Redwood config to new key ARN/alias.
- 2025-02-18 14:25Z: Rolled restart of core services.
- 2025-02-18 14:32Z: First decrypt errors observed.
- 2025-02-18 15:05Z: Disabled previous key in AWS KMS console.

Symptoms observed (logs)
1) Data plane decrypt failures (example)
- service: redwood-dataplane
- pod: dataplane-7f7bb4d9df-qx9lv

2025-02-18T14:37:12.944Z ERROR encrypt.kms decrypt failed request_id=dp-8f2a0c5c tenant=bankofnorthlake err="kms: Decrypt: operation error KMS: Decrypt, https response error StatusCode: 400, RequestID: 0f6b7f8e-7c9c-44a2-b4d7-0f1b2e2a8c7c, api error DisabledException: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:***:key/1a2b3c4d-... is disabled" key_arn="arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:***:key/1a2b3c4d-..." cipher_version=1

2) Control plane decrypt failures for encrypted config blob (example)
- service: redwood-controlplane

2025-02-18T14:41:03.212Z WARN secrets decrypt failed customer=bankofnorthlake err="InvalidCiphertextException: ciphertext was not encrypted under this key" active_kek="alias/bankofnorthlake-redwood-kek" fallback_enabled=false

3) Elevated 500s at gateway
- service: api-gateway

2025-02-18T14:42:55.103Z ERROR upstream 500 route=/v1/chat/completions tenant=bankofnorthlake upstream=dataplane status=500 err="decrypt_failed" trace_id=2f7c3a1b0e4d4b9b

Initial hypothesis
- Rotation was completed without a dual-read window (decrypt-new-then-old) and the previous key was disabled before all ciphertext (and/or wrapped DEKs) were migrated/re-encrypted.
- Intermittent behavior explained by DEK caching: hot pods were serving from cache, while cold/restarted pods had to call KMS Decrypt for wrapped DEKs; those calls failed once the old KEK was disabled.

Immediate mitigation
- Re-enable the previous AWS KMS key (or restore key policy/enable state) to restore decrypt capability for pre-rotation ciphertext.
- Temporarily reduce rollout churn (pause restarts/autoscaling if possible) while stabilizing.

Root cause (most likely)
- Customer disabled the prior KEK too early, and their Redwood Private build/config did not have dual-read bounded fallback enabled for rotation. As a result:
  - ciphertext created pre-rotation could only be decrypted with the old key
  - some services attempted decrypt only using the new key reference
  - when cache missed, KMS Decrypt against old key failed due to DisabledException

Resolution / outcome
- Customer re-enabled the previous key, restoring decrypt for existing ciphertext.
- Support provided an updated rotation procedure emphasizing staged dual-read and a minimum safe window before disabling old keys.
- Customer pinned configuration to a stable alias and validated KMS permissions via preflight checks.

Follow-ups
- Recommend customer upgrade to a release including key-version pinning validation and dual-read support (see related PRs) and to adopt the Private KMS rotation procedure page.
- Internal: feed learnings into docs and installer preflight checks (ENG-4242) and rotation workflow (ENG-4230).
comments:
2025-02-18 15:02Z — Colin O'Donnell (Support)
Customer (Bank of Northlake) reports intermittent 500s after rotating customer-managed AWS KMS key for Private deployment. They updated Helm values for KMS and restarted pods; shortly after, decrypt errors started. Requesting guidance + confirmation of safe rotation steps.

Asks from customer:
- Can we disable the prior key immediately after cutover?
- Do we need to re-encrypt existing secrets/config?
- How to validate rotation is “complete”?

2025-02-18 15:18Z — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Triage: this matches expected failure mode if old KEK is disabled before all services can dual-read (new+old) or before re-encryption/migration. Intermittent nature suggests caching (DEK cache hit -> OK; miss -> KMS decrypt -> fail).

Requested from customer:
- exact timestamps of key disablement
- KMS key ARN(s) + whether alias target changed vs new CMK
- sample logs from dataplane/controlplane around decrypt failures
- whether they enabled any rotation/dual-read flags in values

2025-02-18 15:43Z — Colin O'Donnell (Support)
Customer provided logs showing DisabledException on old key ARN and InvalidCiphertextException when decrypt attempted with new alias target.

Key details:
- They changed the key reference from a specific key ARN to a different key ARN (not only alias target).
- They disabled the previous key ~40 minutes after cutover.
- They did not run any re-encryption job; assumed it was automatic.

2025-02-18 16:05Z — Marcus Lin (Security)
Confirming: envelope encryption requires old KEK to remain available until all wrapped DEKs/ciphertext that reference it are either (a) re-wrapped/re-encrypted, or (b) dual-read remains enabled indefinitely for that historical key set.

Action: advise customer to re-enable old key immediately. Disabling is effectively a destructive operation for decrypt unless you’ve completed migration.

2025-02-18 16:22Z — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Mitigation steps sent to customer (via Support):
1) Re-enable old AWS KMS key (Enabled state) used prior to rotation.
2) Validate KMS IAM/key policy allows kms:Decrypt for BOTH keys for Redwood service role(s).
3) Reduce restarts/autoscaling for next 1–2h to avoid cache churn while stabilized.
4) Collect metrics: rate of decrypt_failed, KMS error codes (DisabledException / AccessDenied / Throttling).

Also pointed them to internal runbook sections (shared excerpt) for KMS dependency degradation toggles (cache TTL, breaker thresholds) but noted those are not a substitute for correct rotation.

2025-02-18 17:12Z — Colin O'Donnell (Support)
Customer confirmed: after re-enabling old key, 500s dropped to baseline within ~5 minutes. Remaining question: how to proceed with rotation safely without downtime.

2025-02-19 10:30Z — Hanae Suzuki (Security Eng)
Provided recommended safe rotation workflow for Private (high level):
- Use a stable alias for KEK reference; do not hardcode key ARN in app config unless you also pin versions explicitly.
- Stage 1: configure new key as “preferred for encrypt” while retaining ability to decrypt with old key (dual-read window).
- Stage 2: run re-encryption / re-wrap pass (where applicable) until audit/metrics indicate no decrypts using old key for N days.
- Stage 3: only then disable old key.

Noted doc gap: customer followed an older internal snippet that did not call out dual-read window explicitly.

2025-02-20 14:05Z — Rafael Mendes (SRE)
Added internal note: this is an example we should incorporate into the failure-mode test harness and docs.

Suggest linking to:
- ADR-0142 for backward-compat/rotation contract
- Private KMS rotation procedure
- Upcoming changes: key-version pinning validation + dual-read bounded fallback (PRs referenced in ticket)

No further customer action required today beyond keeping old key enabled until guided migration is complete.

2025-02-21 09:20Z — Colin O'Donnell (Support)
Customer accepted workaround and planned next steps:
- Keep old key enabled for now
- Upgrade Private deployment to next patch train once available
- Follow updated rotation procedure and run validation checklist

Marking as Resolved; keeping a watch item for any recurrence during their next planned rotation window.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer re-enabled prior AWS KMS key, restoring decrypt capability for pre-rotation ciphertext/wrapped DEKs. Provided updated rotation guidance emphasizing dual-read window and delayed disablement; recommended upgrade to builds supporting key-version pinning validation and rotation-friendly decrypt fallback.
next_steps: Customer: keep old key enabled until migration is verified; follow Private KMS rotation procedure for staged dual-read and validation. Redwood: incorporate learnings into rotation docs and Private installer preflight checks; ensure upcoming releases include safe defaults for rotation (dual-read window + deterministic key selection).
external_links: Customer shared logs (redacted) attached in ticket (see description)
AWS KMS docs: DisabledException / key state behavior (customer-facing reference)
